note: Pieces are named after rhythmic modes and dances rather than songs, so the same names (Binalig, Duyog, Sinulog) recur across albums. Most tracks come from Maguindanao players; the three Lanao tracks are Maranao.

size.basis: No source counts recordings. Discogs lists 99 release hits for 'kulintang', most of them jazz or experimental records using the instrument; the ensemble releases found are about a dozen archive and community albums (Folkways 1961, UP Department of Music Research 1977 and 1988, Lyrichord Maranao volumes c. 1979, World Kulintang Institute 1994, Smithsonian Folkways 2021), each of 10–30 short tracks, plus unreleased archive holdings (Maceda collection) and local Philippine and Sabah recordings. The repertoire itself is small: a handful of Maguindanao rhythmic modes and a dozen-odd Maranao named pieces, so an insider's essential list is about 15 pieces/performances.
